title: Ephemeral key rotation — 401/429 thought notes
content:
Context and high-level notes:
- Investigating odd client errors: intermittent 401s followed by bursts of 429s for some customers (mostly mobile SDKs). Pattern seems distinct from normal rate-limit spikes: often begins right after a successful request that returns a new ephemeral key from our /sessions API.

Observed characteristics (summary):
- Time window: 30s–3m after ephemeral key rotation for affected client sessions.
- Symptom: First failing responses are 401 Unauthorized, then a cascade of 429 Too Many Requests for the same API key.
- Affected routes: generation endpoints and embeddings; seems unrelated to user-level quotas.
- SDKs: mostly Android SDK v1.4.2 and some iOS 2.0.0-beta.
- Geographic spread: US-west + eu-west customers; not isolated to a single region.

Reproduction attempts (what I ran locally / server logs):
1) Simulate rotation flow with curl + manual requests:
- Exchange: POST /sessions/create -> returns ephemeral_key=k_ey123 (expires in 60s)
- Immediately call generation endpoint with new key: curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer k_ey123' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -> success
- Wait ~25s, call again -> got 401 {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"Key revoked"} (server time 2026-03-05T17:14:42Z)
- Subsequent requests from same client -> 429 {"error":"rate_limit","details":"token-use-window-exceeded"}

2) Captured server-side edge logs for a customer (timestamps):
- 2026-03-05 17:14:10 session.create uid=acct-143 key=k_abc123
- 2026-03-05 17:14:12 generate reqid=xyz status=200 key=k_abc123
- 2026-03-05 17:14:42 auth: token invalidated key=k_abc123 reason=rotation
- 2026-03-05 17:14:43 generate reqid=xyz2 status=401 key=k_abc123
- 2026-03-05 17:14:45 generate reqid=xyz3 status=429 key=k_abc123

Hypotheses (ranked quick):
A) Race between rotation invalidation and token cache propagation: the key gets rotated server-side, but some internal caches treat the key as still valid for a short period causing mismatched state that triggers a 401 then invokes per-key fallback which maps to a throttled code path producing 429s.
B) Ephemeral key reuse + global rate-window accounting: when a new key is minted, we create a fresh bucket. If old key is revoked but not fully cleaned up in the billing/rate system, requests get routed to an interim handler that uses remaining quota incorrectly and returns 429.
C) SDKs reusing old key headers during rotation handshake: observed some SDK versions doing parallel requests using old + new keys; backend detects oddness and applies stricter limits (defensive rate limiting) -> 429.
D) Clock skew + expiring TTL check: keys apparently have short TTLs; if client clock drifts, server may consider key expired -> 401, then client retries repeatedly (backoff missing) and exhausts some per-account burst -> 429.

Commands and checks to run next (executable):
- grep -n "token invalidated" /var/log/proxy/* | tail -n50 -> find correlated rotation events and identify servers with delayed cache invalidation.
- curl sequence to simulate parallel requests: run small script that spins two threads: one obtains new key and makes 5 simultaneous requests while the other tries reusing old key. Record diffs.
- Query rate-limit store for key/window after rotation: REDIS> HGETALL rl:account:acct-143:window:20260305T1714 -> check entries for old/new keyIDs.
- Inspect CDN edge-cache TTL for auth header checks: ensure auth header is validated at origin not at edge incorrectly.

Quick pseudo repro script (bash):
# create new session
KEY=$(curl -s -X POST https://control.redwood.ai/v1/sessions -d '{"account":"acct-143"}' | jq -r .ephemeral_key)
# fire two parallel requests: one with KEY and another reusing the previously saved OLD_KEY
OLD_KEY=k_old_test
( curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & )
( curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $OLD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & )
wait

Server response examples captured: 
- 401 body: {"error":"authentication_failed","message":"API key invalid (rotated)","code":"auth.invalid_key"}
- 429 body: {"error":"rate_limit","message":"Too many requests","retry_after":3,"code":"quota.token_rate_window"}

Notes on backend components to inspect:
- Auth service (authz) event stream: Are we emitting "revoke" events and do consumers ack them? Ensure consumer lag in kafka is < 5s.
- Redis rate-limiter: Does it key on account id or key id? Check TTL behavior when key ids are swapped.
- Edge-proxies (Fastly/CloudFront) config: do we cache any responses or auth status? Look for any stale 401->cached leading to weird client behavior.
- SDK client: look for immediate retry loops without exponential backoff during key refresh.

Mitigation ideas (short term):
- Add server-side short holdback window: after rotation, mark old key as "deprecated" for X seconds and return 403 with explicit header X-Deprecated-Until so SDKs can backoff gracefully instead of triggering rate-limit fallback.
- Force clients to complete rotation handshake (single authorized key at a time) by changing session API to return rotation nonce; require client confirm. Risk: more breaking.
- On detection of rotation race in auth service, prefer returning 401 with Retry-After rather than letting rate-limiter kick in.

Next steps / owner suggestions:
- Diego: check kafka consumer lag and authz revoke topic offsets (priority).
- Priya: audit redis rate-limiter key schema + TTL interplay for account vs key-id.
- Me (Maya): produce reproducible script and coordinate with the Android SDK owner to run on staging devices.

Open questions:
- Are there customers using custom proxies that might be replaying Authorization headers?
- Do we rotate keys automatically or on-demand for certain plans? (affects rotation cadence)
- What's the authoritative source for per-token rate windows (auth service vs rate service)?

Rough timeline to resolution estimate: 3–5 days to reproduce + confirm; 1–2 weeks for safe mitigation rollout (holdback header + SDK patch).

Random small notes / breadcrumbs I left for myself: 
- Check GH PR 753: contains a previous edge TTL change that might be related.
- Slack thread #infra-auth: look for "rotation storm" messages dated 2026-02-28.
- Add a short e2e test in staging that does: rotate key -> run 50 small requests across 60s -> assert no 429 burst.

End of scratchpad.
